data.title: Fractyl Health Faces Nasdaq Delisting, Plans Reverse Split
data.description:
Fractyl Health, Inc. ( (GUTS) ) just unveiled an update.

On March 13, 2026, Fractyl Health, Inc. was notified by Nasdaq that its common stock had fallen out of compliance with the minimum $1.00 bid price requirement after trading below that threshold for 30 consecutive business days. After the company failed to regain compliance during the 180‑day grace period that ended September 9, 2026, Nasdaq informed Fractyl on September 10, 2026, that its securities were subject to delisting unless it requested a hearing before a Nasdaq Hearings Panel.

Fractyl Health plans to promptly seek a hearing, which will automatically stay any suspension or delisting and allow its stock to continue trading on Nasdaq while the process is underway. To support efforts to restore compliance, the company filed a proxy statement on August 24, 2026, requesting shareholder approval for a reverse stock split in a ratio between 1‑for‑5 and 1‑for‑15, aiming to lift the share price above the required $1.00 threshold for the period specified by Nasdaq rules.

data.title: NET Power Restructures Oxy-Combustion Partnership With Baker Hughes
data.description:
The latest update is out from NET Power ( (NPWR) ).

On September 8, 2026, NET Power and Baker Hughes affiliates executed a set of integrated agreements that indefinitely suspend their joint development and commercialization programs for utility-scale oxy-combustion power plants while amending an existing license for industrial-scale applications. The move stems from changing market and economic conditions and NET Power’s conclusion that continuing the specific utility-scale turboexpander and platform programs is not currently economical.

Under the new arrangements, performance under the Amended and Restated Joint Development Agreement and the Commercial Agreement is frozen for an indefinite period, and Baker Hughes’ special access and exclusivity rights over NET Power’s La Porte, Texas demonstration facility are terminated. At the same time, Baker Hughes’ Nuovo Pignone affiliates retain exclusive rights to utility-scale equipment packages and gain revised, largely royalty-based industrial licensing terms, though no party is obligated to deploy plants and no royalty amounts are set or assured.

The transaction aligns with NET Power’s previously disclosed strategy not to fund further development of the Oxy-Combustion Cycle, following a $193.7 million non-cash impairment recorded in the quarter ended June 30, 2026 that reduced the carrying amount of its developed oxy-combustion technology and the La Porte facility to zero. data.title: Telecom Argentina Partially Cleared in Tucumán Appeals Ruling Over 2015 Service Outage
data.description:
Telecom Argentina ( (TEO) ) has provided an announcement.

On September 11, 2026, Telecom Argentina reported that the Federal Court of Appeals of Tucumán had issued a ruling in a long-running consumer lawsuit over a service outage on March 3, 2015. The case was brought by Asociación de Consumidores del NOA against Telecom Personal S.A. under Argentina’s Consumers’ Defense Law, challenging the company’s handling of the outage and seeking compensation for affected users.

The appeals court confirmed the lower court’s rejection of compensatory liability claims against Telecom Argentina, meaning the company will not owe broader damages for the 2015 disruption. However, it reversed the earlier denial of proportional reimbursement, requiring that users receive a refund for the portion of service not provided during the outage, which may result in limited financial impact while reinforcing consumer protection standards in the telecom sector.
